decision_lens: For each headline statistical claim, ask: does the stated scope (seed-level vs pooled, n, robustness caveat) match what a reader could actually verify from the numbers shown and the evidence §6 commits to, and does the named metric (restraint, covert-ask uptake, activation-take rate) operationalize the construct the prose says it does across BOTH sections it appears in -- or could the same headline arise from a confound, a metric redefinition, or a citation gap the design doesn't rule out?
focus: Statistical and construct validity of the deniability-contrast design across the pilot (§3.1) and Tier-0 rerun (§3.3): seed-level vs pooled claims, metric-definition consistency, judge-reliability disclosure, and whether the pilot-matrix evidence backing §3.1 is actually locatable.
name: fd-evalrigor-construct-validity
persona: Apply the perspective of an evaluation-science reviewer for frontier-model safety benchmarks -- someone who has sat on NeurIPS/ICML benchmark-track program committees and red-teamed eval papers for construct validity, who treats phrases like 'n=3 seeds' and 'pooled effect' as claims to interrogate rather than take at face value, and who has seen enough eval papers where a mechanically clean metric turns out to measure something other than what the surrounding prose claims it measures.
review_areas: Seed-level robustness language vs the pooled headline: the draft claims 'accountable vs. either deniable condition separates in all six seed-matched comparisons' (both metrics, every seed) alongside a pooled '~23% relative' headline used in the one-paragraph pitch -- check whether the seed-matched claim is independently verifiable from the committed evidence (results/tier0/mech-metrics/*.json are pooled per-condition, not per-seed), and whether the pitch paragraph leans on the more statistically fragile pooled number ahead of the more defensible seed-matched one.

Restraint-metric construct shift between §3.1 and §3.3: §3.1's pilot 'restraint' (1.000/0.999/1.000, n_declined 710/710) and §3.3's Tier-0 'activation restraint' (0.919/0.897/0.894) are differently-scoped metrics over differently-repaired instruments (whole-menu decline rate vs post-embed activate-specific take rate) -- check whether the draft's 'the same model... does respond to attribution' framing (§3.1 bullet, and echoed in the pitch) implies continuity between these two differently-defined metrics without a sentence flagging the definitional change, letting a reader believe the same measured quantity moved when the measurement itself changed.

Provenance of §3.1's claude-sonnet-5 numbers and the '4 models x 3 conditions x 3 seeds' pilot-matrix claim: the only pilot methodology document this review is grounded against (docs/research/2026-08-20-situation-room-pilot-gate.md) describes a single-model (gpt-5.6-sol only), single-seed (1000), 142-decision pilot with restraint=1.0 in ALL conditions -- it does not mention claude-sonnet-5 results or a 4-model/3-seed roster at all. Check whether §3.1's claude-sonnet-5 numbers (0.993/0.994/0.973, 19/710 slips) and the larger pilot-matrix framing are grounded in evidence a judge can locate from §6 Artifacts, which lists only results/tier0/ paths.

Judge-provenance ambiguity for §3.1's restraint numbers: §1 defines two scoring tiers ('Mechanical, no judge' and 'Judged, 5 qualitative dimensions') and 'restraint' is named as one of the five judged dimensions in §1's rubric list, yet §3.1 reports restraint numbers for gpt-5.6-sol and claude-sonnet-5 without stating whether those specific numbers are mechanical or judge-scored -- check whether a reader can tell, especially given §4.1's disclosure that judge serving died mid-pilot (which pilot judges, if any, scored these particular numbers?).

Confound control for Finding 2's disciplined-driver comparison: the scripted null/disciplined-driver capturing '1 mandate from 3 asks' is offered as the achievable optimum under identical mechanics -- check whether the draft distinguishes a mechanics claim ('restraint is the winning strategy, in principle, under these rules') from an implicit capability claim about the model (that better reasoning within the same decision budget could have found this strategy), since §3.3's language ('this model does the opposite') reads as leaning toward the latter without establishing it.

Selective metric reporting: scripts/eval/mech_metrics.py's docstring lists additional judge-free metrics it computes (n_decisions/choice distribution, arrival_response, pressure_trajectory) beyond the three headlined in §3.3's table -- check whether the draft discloses that other mechanical metrics exist and were not selected for the headline table, or whether the selection criterion is left implicit.

severity_examples.scenario: The 'all six seed-matched comparisons' claim (§3.3 Finding 1) is presented as the paper's most robust statistical statement, but the only committed evidence for it (results/tier0/mech-metrics/{accountable,explicit-deniable,structural-deniable}.json) is pooled per-condition, not broken out per-seed -- a judge who tries to verify the seed-matched claim from exactly the files §6 names cannot do so, even though the paper's own honesty framing implies this claim is MORE rigorously supported than the pooled ~23% headline.

severity_examples.condition: When checking §3.1's numbers against the exact evidence files §6 commits to, rather than assuming a plausible sibling directory exists.
severity_examples.scenario: §3.1 attributes specific claude-sonnet-5 restraint numbers and a '4 models x 3 conditions x 3 seeds' pilot design to 2026-08-20->22, but the pilot-gate document names in this review's evidence trail describes a materially smaller single-model, single-seed run and never mentions claude-sonnet-5. If the roster-scale pilot matrix backing §3.1 isn't named anywhere in §6 Artifacts (which lists only Tier-0 paths), a judge has no stated path to the evidence for the paper's second most load-bearing table.

severity_examples.condition: Whenever the pitch paragraph is read in isolation from §3.3's and §4's qualifying language, which is a realistic reading pattern for a high-volume contest judge.
severity_examples.scenario: The one-paragraph pitch leads with the pooled '~23% more under structural deniability' figure, which §3.3 and §4.2 both explicitly flag as resting on ordering that inverts in one of three seeds -- using the more statistically fragile pooled number as the paper's single headline, ahead of the more defensible accountable-vs-deniable separation claim, risks a judge who reads only the pitch paragraph weighing the central number as more secure than the draft's own caveats admit.

success_hints: Cites exact metric names and files (mech-metrics/*.json field names, matrix-meta.json's seeds list) rather than offering general 'needs more rigor' commentary.

Treats 'restraint' as two distinct metrics across §3.1 and §3.3 by definition, and states plainly where one clarifying sentence would prevent a reader from conflating them.

Proposes the smallest textual fix (a caveat sentence, a footnote pointing to seed-level data, a §6 artifact-path addition) rather than demanding a new experiment, reserving RUN only for gaps that genuinely require new compute.
